page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, AES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. The instance is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There are no integrated GPUs or local storage drives bundled with this server, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores. Single-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 7120.47 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 226.16 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier results in software compilation with Clang and image processing, while maintaining strong performance in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reached 112.7 million operations per second.

The server presents a balanced profile for memory-heavy workloads, offering high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance without the added cost of bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. However, the lack of local storage requires external disk attachment, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 perform at average levels. Additionally, while LLM inference for small and medium models is strong to top-tier, performance drops to average levels for large 70B models. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
